ce_bugs.text: In Hubspot's CalendarService, the fetch Response is typed as HubspotToken, so accessToken/expiresIn reads yield undefined/NaN, persisting a garbage credential that fails downstream API calls with confusing auth errors

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses a plain z.object which strips unknown keys from the parsed output, so the sync response's expiry_date is dropped, causing office365 (which merges tokenResponse.data into credentials) to fail advancing the expiry and attempt a refresh on every API call

parseRefreshTokenResponse switches to the minimum schema based on the sharing flag even when the response did not come from the sync endpoint, causing Salesforce responses (which come straight from login.salesforce.com) to be stripped of instance_url, signature, and scope from the stored credential
Webhook handler's JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throws unhandled if the payload is malformed or the encryption key mismatches
Webhook handler has no req.method === 'POST' check, so a GET with no body hits the schema parse and 500s
Webhook secret is compared with !== (non-constant-time) on an endpoint that can overwrite arbitrary users' app credentials, instead of using crypto.timingSafeEqual
A webhook header-name env variable containing uppercase characters will silently never match Node's lowercased headers, breaking secret lookup

The outbound credential-sync POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication (no shared secret or signature) yet returns live OAuth access tokens, letting anyone who can reach the endpoint mint credentials for any known userId
Webhook find-then-create credential logic is not atomic, so two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both create credentials, leaving duplicate credentials with stale tokens

Office365 lost its diagnostic path on failed token parse: previously it logged the Zod error and raw Microsoft response and degraded gracefully to old credentials, but now throws a generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' with no context
In sharing mode, minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys [z.string().toString()] evaluate to literal '[object Object]' key, so Zod strips all fields except access_token from parsed output
In sharing mode, missing refresh_token is backfilled with placeholder string 'refresh_token' and persisted, destroying the user's real refresh token and requiring re-authentication
In sharing mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns raw fetch Response but Google CalendarService caller accesses res?.data causing TypeError since only Gaxios responses have .data
HubSpot call site has same type mismatch risk: HubspotToken type assertion applied to a raw Response object
Webhook persists attacker-supplied decrypted JSON into credential.key with no Zod schema validation, enabling type-confusion in downstream token handling
Webhook endpoint leaks user existence via distinct 404 'User not found' errors to holders of the shared secret
JSON.parse/decrypt failures in webhook are unhandled, causing uncaught 500 errors
Webhook secret comparison uses !== instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual, enabling theoretical timing-based byte-by-byte secret recovery

Google Calendar token refresh stores the safeParse result wrapper ({ success, data }) instead of the parsed key object, corrupting the credential so future parsing fails and breaks the integration permanently until re-auth

In Google Calendar sync mode, the minimum schema strips refresh_token from data and the mutation in parseRefreshTokenResponse replaces the real token with the literal string "refresh_token" before storage

parseRefreshTokenResponse silently replaces missing refresh tokens with the literal string "refresh_token", persisting a placeholder over the credential's actual refresh token and destroying data with no recovery except re-auth

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString() which collapse to the string "[object Object]", so both keys collide and expiry validation never happens, allowing responses without expiry to be accepted and persisted

refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response when sync is enabled, but Zoho/HubSpot callers access .data as an axios response (undefined on fetch Response), breaking all Zoho/HubSpot flows in the sync-enabled configuration

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParseReturnType wrapper ({ success, data }) instead of the parsed data, so credential.key is persisted with a wrapper shape that fails schema validation on next read, breaking Google Calendar integration with no migration for existing credentials (CalendarService.ts:94)

parseRefreshTokenResponse clobbers refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" and strips fields in sharing mode, permanently destroying Office365's real refresh token and making credentials unrecoverable without re-auth
For Salesforce in sharing mode, the stored key loses instance_url, signature, and scope (required fields stripped by minimumTokenResponseSchema), breaking subsequent jsforce.Connection usage
Salesforce direct fetch bypasses the credential-sync endpoint while parseRefreshTokenResponse still honors it, creating a mixed contract

parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on validation failure, changing the error-handling contract: Office365 previously logged errors and continued, and Zoom's !parsedToken.success handling path is now unreachable dead code, causing transient bad refresh responses to hard-fail booking flows

Zoho Bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects a Cal.com user ID, so the sync endpoint receives a credential ID labeled as a user ID and fails to resolve the user (zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:85)
Outbound credential-sync request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no auth header (e.g., CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET), so the receiving application cannot verify the sender
No response.ok check on the credential-sync fetch response before the body is consumed and persisted as credential data
New webhook endpoint (app-credential.ts) has no req.method === "POST" restriction on an endpoint that writes credentials
Webhook secret comparison uses !== instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual on an endpoint that can overwrite arbitrary users' app credentials if brute-forced
Webhook handler throws unhandled errors from appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and JSON.parse of decrypted keys, producing generic 500s leaking zod error details instead of 400s

.env.example documents an AES-256 key as 'must be 32 bytes' but recommends openssl rand -base64 24, which produces 24 bytes, causing self-hosters' keys to fail symmetricDecrypt or derive the wrong key

refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response object that doesn't match any caller's expected shape, causing TypeErrors or undefined property access (e.g., res?.data, expiresIn) in all wrapped calendar services when sync is enabled
The sync response is never .json()-parsed before being returned to callers
refreshOAuthTokens has no response.ok check, so a 500 from the sync endpoint flows through as a successful Response

parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the literal sentinel string "refresh_token" into persisted credentials when the provider's refresh response omits refresh_token, causing permanent refresh failure until re-authentication

The sync endpoint request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is completely unauthenticated — no secret header or signature — allowing anyone who learns the URL to obtain fresh OAuth access tokens for any user ID

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses garbage computed keys like [z.string().toString()], so the expiry validation is dead code and responses missing expiry data pass validation, persisting undefined/NaN expiry dates
Webhook handler's symmetricDecrypt throws unhandled when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset or misconfigured, causing a 500
Webhook handler's JSON.parse on the decrypted blob throws unhandled, causing a 500
Webhook handler writes the decrypted keys object into credential.key with no schema validation, so a malformed payload permanently corrupts the user's credential
Salesforce uses response.statusText !== "OK" as a success check, which is unreliable because statusText can be empty on HTTP/2 responses, causing a successful response to throw HttpError 400
Zoho Bigin passes credentialId where every other call site passes credential.userId, so the sync endpoint receives a credential ID as calcomUserId and token refresh matches the wrong entity

O365 error-handling regression: parse failure now throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" with no try/catch in refreshAccessToken, aborting the refresh entirely instead of degrading gracefully as before
Webhook secret is compared with !== (not constant-time), leaking secret length/prefix via timing; should use crypto.timingSafeEqual
Webhook header name lookup is case-sensitive against Node's lowercased header names, so an uppercase CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME value causes a 403 on every webhook with no obvious cause

Sync mode in parseRefreshTokenResponse ignores the caller-supplied schema parameter and replaces it with the minimum schema, stripping provider-specific required fields like Salesforce's instance_url before persistence

Placeholder literal string 'refresh_token' is inserted as a real credential value in sync mode after the minimum schema strips the actual refresh_token, causing later refresh attempts to send the sentinel string to Google
Zoho Bigin adapter passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, causing the sync endpoint to receive the wrong calcomUserId and write credentials for the wrong user
Webhook handler uses unguarded z.parse without try/catch or defaultHandler/defaultResponder wrapper, throwing a ZodError as an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 on invalid body
Webhook handler has no req.method === 'POST' check, allowing any HTTP verb to reach the mutation logic

Salesforce refresh path bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely and always calls login.salesforce.com directly, diverging from the pattern of six other adapters and hitting the worst of both branches in sync mode
Outbound sync fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication (no CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header or credential), leaving the receiving side with no way to authenticate the request
Google Calendar stores the Zod SafeParseReturnType object as the credential key instead of the parsed value, corrupting credentials on the default non-sync path (CalendarService.ts:96)

The minimum Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed keys '[z.string().toString()]' producing the key '[object Object]', validates nothing, and strips unknown fields so safeParse data only contains access_token (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-8)
Fake 'refresh_token' literal string is persisted as the token value when parsed data lacks it, overwriting the real stored refresh token for office365 and zoom (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:22-24)

Salesforce in sync mode parses its real response with the hollowed-out minimum schema, stripping instance_url and other required fields and breaking the jsforce connection (salesforce CalendarService.ts:84-95)
Webhook endpoint accepts any HTTP method and lets Zod errors from parsing undefined bodies surface as unhandled 500s with stack traces instead of guarded 400/405 responses (app-credential.ts:17-32)
Webhook uses timing-unsafe plain string comparison for the secret instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual, and mishandles array headers where a duplicate header value is rejected (app-credential.ts:21-27)
TOCTOU race in webhook's findFirst-then-update/create flow allows duplicate (userId, appId) credentials and nondeterministic target row updates (app-credential.ts:62-92)
zoho-bigin passes credentialId as the userId parameter to refreshOAuthTokens, causing sync lookups to target the wrong user (zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts:90-97)

mrv_findings.text: .env.example:241 documents `openssl rand -base64 24` for the AES-256 key, which produces 24 bytes instead of the required 32 bytes, causing aes-256-cbc to throw 'Invalid key length' and breaking the credential-sync webhook handler; should be `openssl rand -base64 32`

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-9 uses computed zod keys from `z.string().toString()` which evaluate to the literal string "ZodString", collapsing both keys and overwriting the first, so the schema strips all fields except access_token including the expiry, causing token refresh loops on every request

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:23-25 writes the placeholder literal string "refresh_token" into real credentials when the sync-endpoint response omits refresh_token, permanently breaking the credential when the next refresh sends the nonsense value

CalendarService.ts:95 (googlecalendar) stores the zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper (`{success, data, error}`) instead of the parsed data as the credential key, corrupting every Google credential that passes through token refresh

CalendarService.ts:86-91 (googlecalendar) in sync mode treats the raw fetch Response returned by refreshOAuthTokens as an already-parsed token object, so `res?.data` is undefined and every token refresh throws TypeError reading 'access_token'; response.ok is never checked

CalendarService.ts:177-187 (hubspot) assigns the fetch Response to HubspotToken in sync mode, so expires_in is undefined producing NaN expiry and refresh_token: undefined is persisted, permanently destroying the HubSpot credential

zoho-bigin and zohocrm CalendarService read `tokenInfo.data.error`/`tokenInfo.data.expiryDate` from refreshOAuthTokens output, but in sync mode it returns a fetch Response with no `.data`, causing TypeError on every token refresh under sync mode

zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts:93 passes `credentialId` where refreshOAuthTokens requires a `userId`, sending the credential ID as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint and potentially cross-wiring credentials between users

app-credential.ts:43 looks up `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` but appStoreMetadata is keyed by app-store directory names while App.slug uses hyphenated slugs, so most apps return 404 'App not found' even though the DB lookup succeeded; lookup must match on metadata.slug

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod safeParse wrapper ({success, data, error}) instead of the parsed credential, and the wrapper object is persisted as credential.key, corrupting the stored Google credential on the first token refresh for every user

In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, z.string().toString() evaluates to the literal string '[object Object]', collapsing both computed keys into one garbage optional key so the minimum schema only requires access_token and expiry_date is never validated

Because z.object strips unknown keys in sync mode, refreshTokenResponse.data has no refresh_token, so the code always sets refresh_token to the literal string 'refresh_token', which Zoom persists as a real refresh token, permanently breaking the credential
In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the Google caller reads res?.data causing token.access_token to throw TypeError
In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but HubSpot types it as HubspotToken and persists undefined/NaN as the credential's refresh_token and expiry
In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but Lark feeds it to handleLarkError which expects Lark's {code, msg} error envelope
app-credential.ts webhook uses .parse instead of safeParse on the request body with no method check, so malformed bodies or GET requests throw ZodError and return 500 instead of 400
app-credential.ts webhook does no runtime check that CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is 32 bytes, so a blank/wrong-length key or non-JSON ciphertext throws an unhandled exception

app-credential.ts webhook persists decrypted keys to credential.key with no validation against the target app's credential schema, accepting arbitrary garbage JSON as a working credential and returning 200

zoho-bigin CalendarService passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint looks up the wrong or nonexistent user and returns tokens for the wrong identity

app-credential.ts webhook uses prisma.credential.findFirst with no ordering when users have multiple credentials for the same app, so syncing one account silently overwrites an arbitrary other credential, and the request schema has no field to disambiguate
SalesforceCalendarService refreshes tokens directly against login.salesforce.com instead of going through refreshOAuthTokens, bypassing the CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT contract
SalesforceCalendarService refreshes on every service instantiation with no expiry check, triggering a token refresh and DB write on every booking/availability operation
SalesforceCalendarService uses response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok, which is fragile since some proxies return empty statusText
The outbound sync request in refreshOAuthTokens sends no authentication credentials, so the sync endpoint cannot verify the request came from this Cal.com instance
The outbound sync request in refreshOAuthTokens has no response.ok check or timeout, so 4xx/5xx errors from the parent application are passed downstream and surface as confusing parse errors

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts: z.string().toString() is not a dynamic-key expression; both computed keys evaluate to the constant '[object Object]', so the 'minimum' schema strips all properties except access_token, silently discarding expiry_date, expires_in, and provider-specific fields

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts: because refresh_token is stripped by the broken schema, the function fabricates and injects the literal string 'refresh_token' as the refresh token, destroying persisted credentials after one refresh cycle

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts: the token-stripping degraded path is gated on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED alone, conflating the inbound webhook feature with the outbound sync feature, so self-hosters enabling only the webhook get token-stripping applied to normal provider refreshes

refreshOAuthTokens.ts: the sync path returns a raw unparsed fetch Response, but all call sites were wired to consume the original provider's return shape (e.g. googlecalendar reads res?.data which is undefined on a fetch Response), causing TypeError on first refresh; larkcalendar and hubspot call sites similarly break
refreshOAuthTokens.ts: the sync branch was added to eleven apps but response adaptation was implemented for zero of them, leaving no functioning requirement path

salesforce CalendarService.ts: unconditional token refresh and persistence added for all Salesforce users without gating on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED or CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, changing default behavior (jsforce previously refreshed lazily in memory only on auth failure)
salesforce CalendarService.ts: transient Salesforce/token endpoint failures now throw HttpError and break calendar operations that previously succeeded with the still-valid stored token

salesforce CalendarService.ts: error check response.statusText !== 'OK' rejects responses whose reason phrase differs (e.g. 'Created' or empty) regardless of 2xx status; response.ok should be enforced instead

app-credential.ts webhook: writes decrypted keys to credential.key with no app-specific zod schema validation, unlike every other credential-write path, so malformed or schema-mismatched sync payloads silently replace working credentials with no validation error or rollback
app-credential.ts webhook: accepts any appSlug present in appStoreMetadata, allowing the sync side to overwrite credentials for apps never part of the sync design, broader than the stated intent

zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts: passes credentialId as the third argument to refreshOAuthTokens where calcomUserId is required (every other call site passes credential.userId), causing the sync endpoint to look up the wrong user or none when sync is enabled

zoho-bigin api/add.ts: unrelated drive-by change replaces config-driven appConfig.slug with hardcoded 'zoho-bigin' in the OAuth redirect URI, causing the redirect URI to silently diverge from the registered callback route if the config slug ever changes

CalendarService.ts stores raw zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper as credential key instead of parsed data, corrupting Google credentials after first refresh and permanently breaking Google Calendar

refreshOAuthTokens sync path returns un-parsed fetch Response but call sites expect provider-specific objects (Google res.data, HubSpot SDK object, Zoho axios response), causing TypeErrors and dead-on-arrival sync for Google/HubSpot/Zoho

parseRefreshTokenResponse writes sentinel string 'refresh_token' into the credential as if it were a real token when provider omits it, combined with schema stripping causing loss of all other stored credential fields

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-16 — shared-mode branch returns a raw fetch Response instead of the Gaxios/axios-style response with .data expected by callers in googlecalendar, hubspot, zohocrm, and zoho-bigin CalendarService, causing TypeErrors and undefined token fields when credential sharing is enabled

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-10 — computed schema keys z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() both evaluate to "[object Object]" so the second overwrites the first, making the expiry-validation requirement dead code and stripping expiry_date, expires_in, scope etc. from parsed tokens (breaking Office365 expiry tracking)

app-credential.ts:74-80 — credential update replaces the entire key JSON wholesale without merging, so a partial sync payload silently destroys existing fields like refresh_token, scope, and instance_url
